subject: Post-call: Clarifying data flow, telemetry subprocessors, and next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@finfoundry.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Clarifying data flow, telemetry subprocessors, and next steps

Hi Daniel — thanks again for the intro call earlier today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope an internal gating checklist: 

Recap from our side:
- You plan to integrate Redwood via the marketplace flow and also ship lightweight client-side telemetry for usage metrics.
- Priority is EU data residency for European customers; a small subset of support logs may be routed to a US-based analytics vendor for product analytics.
- You asked about retention options and our ability to limit which telemetry fields are sent.

Asks / clarifying questions (can reply inline):
1) For PII: can you confirm the concrete fields you consider PII (examples: full name, email, account_id, raw prompts)?
2) Data residency: which product traffic must remain in EU by law or policy vs. what can be processed in other regions?
3) Subprocessors: you mentioned you use PulseMetrics for analytics — can you share the contract/vendor name and the expected data they will receive?
4) Log retention: approximate retention windows you need for full logs vs aggregated metrics.
5) Marketplace flow: will customer data ever egress to a marketplace partner (cloud provider or partner analytics) as part of billing/usage aggregation?

I've attached a short telemetry questionnaire (redwood-telemetry-questionnaire.pdf) to make it easy to answer. Once you send the vendor list + dataflow diagram we can do a quick internal security/legal gating and propose a minimal set of contract language.

Proposed next steps:
- You: share vendor list + data flow diagram and PII field examples by end of week
- Us: we’ll run an internal evaluation (security + legal + product) and come back with a minimal gating checklist and suggested DPA redlines in 3 business days after receiving materials

If it helps, we can set a short follow-up demo that includes our Privacy & Security lead.

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber | Enterprise Solutions 
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@finfoundry.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: Clarifying data flow, telemetry subprocessors, and next steps

Thanks Jonas — great summary. Answers inline: 

1) PII: primary keys we consider PII are email, customer_id, and any free-text fields containing customer names or account-specific identifiers. Prompts may include PHI-like snippets; we aim to avoid sending raw prompts where possible.
2) Data residency: EU customers must have request/response and user-identifying logs kept in the EU. Aggregated metrics may be stored in US.
3) Subprocessors: main vendor is PulseMetrics (pulsemetrics.ai) — they receive anonymized event streams and summary metrics today. We're evaluating whether raw traces will be forwarded.
4) Retention: legal requires 90-day access to raw traces for incident investigation; product prefers 30 days. Aggregated metrics: 2 years.
5) Marketplace: initial plan is to use the Azure Marketplace for onboarding in EU, but billing/usage aggregation will likely route to our centralized analytics pipeline which currently sits in us-east (CloudServe / AWS).

Attached: finfoundry-dataflow.png (simple diagram). Procurement loop: procurement@finfoundry.com is on cc for DPA / contracting.

Can you confirm what minimal telemetry fields Redwood needs to operate (latency, error codes, token counts) so we can flag and mask the rest?

—Daniel
Daniel Park | Head of Product
FinFoundry
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@finfoundry.com>, procurement@finfoundry.com
Date: Wed, 23 Jul 2025 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: Clarifying data flow, telemetry subprocessors, and next steps

Hi Ben / Marissa — forwarding Daniel's reply and the dataflow diagram. TL;DR: EU residency for request/response and user-identifying logs; PulseMetrics may receive anonymized events but they might want raw traces for debugging. Retention asks: legal 90d raw, product 30d; aggregated 2y.

Can you advise on our standard gating and minimal contract language? Quick questions for the internal checklist: 
- Is PulseMetrics acceptable if they sign our subprocessor addendum + confirm no persistent PII storage?
- For marketplace onboarding (Azure), what egress constraints should we include to prevent EU customer data from leaving region?
- Do we require HSM-backed KMS for telemetry vendors?

I'll consolidate your guidance into a short email back to FinFoundry and propose a joint call.

Forwarded message follows.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@finfoundry.com>, procurement@finfoundry.com
Date: Wed, 23 Jul 2025 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: Clarifying data flow, telemetry subprocessors, and next steps

Thanks for the context — good questions. Short answers and recommended next steps below.

Short answers:
- PulseMetrics: conditionally acceptable. Require signed subprocessor addendum, SOC 2 Type II report, and a commitment they will not persist raw prompts or unredacted PII.
- Retention: propose we aim for a product compromise: 30 days raw traces for product debugging (encrypted at rest) with a legal-approved 90-day incident retention option that requires escalation and justification. Aggregated metrics at 2 years is fine if they’re non-identifiable.
- Residency/Marketplace: require contractual clause that request/response logs for EU customers are processed and stored in EU regions only. For marketplace onboarding, enforce region pinning or use a regional pod for EU customers. No automatic egress to us-east for EU-marked tenants.
- Encryption/KMS: require TLS in transit and KMS-managed encryption at rest. HSM/KMS recommended for telemetry vendors storing any user-identifiable logs; if vendor refuses, we gate them.

Evidence we need before approving vendor in prod:
1) Vendor list + data flow diagram (we have the diagram but need the vendor-specific flow to PulseMetrics).
2) Vendor security questionnaire + SOC2 Type II (or equivalent).
3) Confirmation on fields being sent (we should get a sample event schema and a promise to mask/strip PII fields).
4) DPA with subprocessor clause and data residency commitments.

Suggested gating playbook (3 steps):
A) Risk assessment (security + legal) using vendor-eval-template.xlsx (attached).
B) Product changes: add telemetry allow-list and drop fields containing PII (Jonas to coordinate with product engineer).
C) Contracting: Marissa/legal to propose DPA redlines including residency, retention, and subprocessor constraints.

I'll take point on the security questionnaire and SOC2 checklist. Marissa, can you draft the DPA redline highlights we want included?

Ben Carter
Head of Security, Redwood Inference

Attachment: vendor-eval-template.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@finfoundry.com>, procurement@finfoundry.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: Clarifying data flow, telemetry subprocessors, and next steps

Thanks — I’ll prepare DPA redline bullets and send a short template by EOD tomorrow. Key items I’ll include: residency clause for EU-marked tenants, retention caps with escalation path for longer retention, prohibition on storing raw prompts, and standard audit rights. Also will request proof of SOC2 and a recent penetration test.

Daniel / procurement: once we share the redlines, Marissa/legal will need a vendor contact who can receive and sign the subprocessor addendum. Please let us know who that is.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
